title: Claiming HRA for Self & Parents: Rules for Your Properties
description: House Rent Allowance (HRA) exemption is available only under the old tax regime. You can claim HRA for rent paid towards the residential accommodation you act.

faq.q: 1. Can I claim HRA if I live in my own house?
faq.a: No, HRA is specifically for rent paid for accommodation you occupy. If you own the house you live in, you cannot claim HRA.

faq.q: 2. Is HRA exemption available under the new tax regime?
faq.a: No, HRA exemption is one of the many deductions and exemptions that are not available if you opt for the new, simplified tax regime.

faq.q: 3. What documents do I need to claim HRA?
faq.a: You typically need rent receipts. If the annual rent paid exceeds ₹1 lakh, you must also provide your landlord's Permanent Account Number (PAN).

faq.q: 4. Can I claim HRA for rent paid to my spouse?
faq.a: No, you cannot claim HRA for rent paid to your spouse. The Income Tax Department generally disallows such claims as they are not considered a genuine landlord-tenant relationship.

faq.q: 5. What if my landlord doesn't have a PAN or refuses to provide it?
faq.a: If the annual rent exceeds ₹1 lakh and your landlord does not have a PAN, you should obtain a declaration from them to that effect, along with their name and address. However, it's generally advisable to deal with landlords who comply with tax regulations.

faq.q: 6. Can I claim HRA if I own a house but live in a rented apartment in the same city?
faq.a: Yes, you can, provided you can justify why you are not living in your own house (e.g., your own house is rented out, or it's far from your workplace). You must also be genuinely paying rent for the apartment you occupy.
